questions.question: When weather, road, or traffic conditions are bad, what is the minimum following distance you should keep?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four seconds.
questions.explanation: When conditions are not ideal, increase your following distance to at least four seconds. This gives you more time to stop.

questions.question: When you turn left onto a one-way street, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The lane closest to your previous lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane that is closest to where you came from. This is the safest way to turn.

questions.question: What do fluorescent yellow-green signs indicate?
questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Fluorescent yellow-green signs warn about schools, pedestrians, and bicycles. Drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow arrow at a traffic signal?

options.text: Merge into the lane the arrow points to.
Turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
Go left because you have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in that direction. But you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians first.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates?

options.text: Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to beat a train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always watch for trains and be prepared to stop. Do not cross until your entire vehicle can clear the tracks. Do not shift gears while crossing because your vehicle might stall.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road joins from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a road is coming in from the right side ahead.

questions.question: In winter, what happens to shaded areas on roads?

options.text: They freeze at the same time as the rest of the road.
They freeze after the rest of the road.
They freeze before the rest of the road.
They thaw before the rest of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They freeze before the rest of the road.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas freeze first and stay icy longer than sunny areas. Be extra careful driving in shadows during winter.

questions.question: How should you use a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Slow down before you enter the ramp.
Slow down after you enter the ramp.
Keep your speed the same on the ramp.
Pass other cars on the ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you enter the ramp.
questions.explanation: Stay at freeway speed until you move onto the exit ramp. Then slow down.

questions.question: When passing a car on a two-lane road, when should you return to your lane?

options.text: When there is enough space between you and the car you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is enough space between you and the car you passed.
questions.explanation: After passing, return to the right lane when you have enough space between your car and the car you passed.

questions.question: What do pentagonal signs indicate?
questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs mark school zones. Watch carefully for children and pedestrians in these areas.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Communicate with other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your emergency signals or horn when needed.

questions.question: What do pennant-shaped signs mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zones.
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs show no passing zones. The sign will also have text that says 'no passing.'

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm points upward, they are signaling a right turn. Adjust your driving if you are following a driver using this signal.

questions.question: You are driving on a highway with two solid yellow lines. When can you cross them?

options.text: Only to turn left into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.
To pass other vehicles if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to turn left into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing in both directions. You may only cross these lines to turn left into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: When parallel parking, how far from the curb can your car be?
questions.correctAnswerText: 18 inches
questions.explanation: Park no more than 18 inches from the curb. Always park where drivers coming from both directions can see your car.

questions.question: Does drinking coffee after drinking alcohol affect your blood alcohol level?

options.text: It has no effect on blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has no effect on blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Coffee does not lower your blood alcohol level. It may keep you awake, but it will not make you sober.

questions.question: What color are guide signs that show directions and distances?
questions.correctAnswerText: Green
questions.explanation: Guide signs have green backgrounds. They show directions and distances to help drivers find their destination.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The maximum or minimum legal speed on a road under bad conditions.
The maximum or minimum legal speed on a road under good conditions.
The recommended speed on a road under good conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum or minimum legal speed on a road under good conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the legal maximum or minimum speed on a road under good conditions. You can drive slower, but not faster. Slow down in school zones, work zones, and bad weather.

questions.question: If your car skids, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: In the direction you want the car to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the car to go.
questions.explanation: Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the car to go. Once the car straightens out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: How can you avoid driving dangerously and aggressively?

options.text: Speed only when there are no police officers nearby.
Make eye contact with aggressive drivers.
Tailgate other drivers to show you need to get somewhere.
Plan enough time for your trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan enough time for your trip.
questions.explanation: Plan ahead so you have plenty of time to reach your destination. If you leave early, you won't feel rushed and won't need to break traffic rules.

questions.question: What are signs called that require drivers to follow an instruction?
questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must or must not do. Breaking these rules can result in a fine.

questions.question: A leaking exhaust system can:

options.text: Require your vehicle to have a tune-up sooner than normal.
Set grass fires on country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make you drowsy while driving.
questions.explanation: A leaky exhaust system releases toxic fumes. These fumes can make you drowsy and are very dangerous.

questions.question: In winter weather, overpasses and bridges:

options.text: Are affected in the same way as other roadways.
Freeze after the rest of the roads.
Freeze before the rest of the roads.
Thaw out before the rest of the roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Freeze before the rest of the roads.
questions.explanation: Bridges and overpasses freeze before other roads and stay icy longer. Drive slowly and carefully on these areas in freezing weather.

questions.question: When approaching an uncontrolled intersection, a driver should:

options.text: Stop at the intersection, check in all directions, and proceed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to yield.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, be ready to yield. Ease off the gas, cover the brake, and check left, right, and left again.

questions.question: Regulatory signs:

options.text: Are placed in every location where there is a present danger.
Indicate what a driver must or must not do.
Are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
May warn drivers that they are approaching a school zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Indicate what a driver must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black lettering on white. They tell drivers what they must or must not do, like speed limits or no passing rules.

questions.question: What color are pavement markings that separate traffic lanes moving in opposite directions?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines in the center of the road separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This circular sign warns you of an upcoming railroad crossing. Watch for trains.

questions.question: If you find that you're in a turn lane but want to drive straight ahead, you should:

options.text: Reverse your vehicle and merge back into traffic.
Put on your turn signal and wait to merge back into through-traffic.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make the turn anyway.
questions.explanation: If you are in a turn lane, make the turn. Other drivers expect you to turn. You can go around the block to return to your original direction.

questions.question: Your vehicle's stopping distance increases when stopping:

options.text: On a wet or icy road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Wet or icy roads increase stopping distance. Loose gravel or stones also increase stopping distance.

questions.question: If you are following an emergency vehicle, your following distance should be a minimum of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Four seconds.
questions.explanation: Stay at least four seconds behind an emergency vehicle. Emergency vehicles need extra space to operate safely.
